hints: Notice that $X$ is the velocity of the plane through the air and $W$ is the velocity of the air past the ground, so the ground velocity $Y$ must be their vector sum.
Recall that to add two vectors you place them head to tail, so the arrow for $X$ followed by the arrow for $W$ must end at the tip of $Y$.
Check each triangle for which two vectors placed head to tail produce the third vector $Y$ as the resultant from start to finish.
walkthrough: Identify the physics: velocity relative to ground equals velocity relative to air plus velocity of air relative to ground, so $Y = X + W$ as vectors.
Recall vector addition: to find $X + W$, place the tail of $W$ at the head of $X$, then the resultant joins the tail of $X$ to the head of $W$.
That resultant must be $Y$, so look for a triangle where starting at the tail of $X$, going along $X$ then along $W$, you arrive at the head of $Y$.
In diagram A, $X$ points up, $W$ starts at the head of $X$ and $Y$ joins the tail of $X$ to the head of $W$, satisfying $X + W = Y$.
The other diagrams join the vectors to give $W + Y = X$ or $X + Y = W$ or use a reversed $Y$.

options.A: Placing $X$ followed by $W$ head to tail gives a resultant from the start of $X$ to the end of $W$, which is $Y$, so $X + W = Y$.
options.B: This triangle gives $W + Y = X$, which would make $X$ the ground velocity instead of the air velocity.
options.C: This parallelogram adds $X$ and $Y$ to give $W$, so $X + Y = W$, which reverses the required vector addition.
options.D: The $Y$ arrow is reversed compared with the correct addition, so the triangle does not satisfy $X + W = Y$.
